channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: People are paying thousands for a home upgrade that’s often unnecessary
item.description: Outdated practices and codes are resulting in costly recommendations for larger electrical panels to add appliances such as induction stoves, heat pumps or EV chargers. Yet such panel upgrades are rarely needed, some researchers say.

item.title: The strange, sordid case of Trump, China and the AI chips
item.description: Democrats, you will soon be in charge of Congress. Rein in this national security mess, Jim Geraghty writes.

item.title: Silicon Valley’s Trump-era playbook is falling apart. A major shift is underway.
item.description: As public anger over AI grows, some tech industry leaders are calling for a sharp break with the build-at-all-costs ethos that dominated President Donald Trump’s Washington.

item.title: Supreme Court allows construction to resume on border security project in Texas that cuts through parts of Big Bend National Park
item.description: The more than 500-mile stretch of road, cameras, vehicle barriers and sensors is planned in and around the park. It is one of the longest and most controversial sections.

item.title: Impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth begins in House, focused on Iran war
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie (R) alleges that Hegseth “abused” his powers and “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” by carrying out strikes against Iran.

item.title: This solution to obesity doesn’t work. America still eats it up.
item.description: Eat better. Exercise. And learn to cook?

item.title: Mississippi ballot deadline looms in tight Senate race, as Democrat Colom’s lead continues to inch upward
item.description: Scott Colom’s margin over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) grew to nearly 2,600 votes Monday, a day before the official cutoff to count provisional ballots and receive absentee ballots.

item.title: Your stroke risk is 72 percent higher during these 3 hours of the day
item.description: The morning rush often feels like nothing short of a crisis. For our hearts and brains, it’s also the riskiest time of day, writes physician Trisha Pasricha.

item.title: Why Republican eye rolls could turn into action against Trump’s foreign policy
item.description: The midterm results could provoke a bipartisan push against the president’s failed foreign policy.

item.title: Republicans push to make the most of their time left in control of Congress
item.description: Congress is scheduled to be in session for five more weeks before the end of the year — but some Republicans in both chambers are urging their colleagues to work weekends and holidays to confirm as many of President Donald Trump’s nominees and pass as much legislation as they can in the lame-duck session before Democrats take control.

item.title: Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assault
item.description: The British actor was convicted of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009.

item.title: Trump says his deportation policies may have been ‘too tough’ in his first TV network interview since the election losses
item.description: On “60 Minutes,” the president was reflective and at times open to collaboration, but simultaneously defensive as he prepares for battle with congressional Democrats.

item.title: 2028 contenders. ‘60 Minutes.’ Pete Hegseth. Nvidia CEO. Biden’s health. Stroke symptoms. Ocean liner. Catch up now.
item.description: Catch up in minutes.

item.title: ‘Love Is Blind’ is actually a documentary about toxic masculinity, our columnist writes
item.description: Rarely have we stood so united in ick as we did this season, according to columnist Michael Andor Brodeur.

item.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about offering press secretary job to UFC’s Dana White, ending a day of speculation
item.description: The president’s comments ended speculation that he had chosen his longtime friend and political ally to fill one of the most high-profile jobs in the White House, as he shakes up his administration following the midterm elections. Trump’s previous pick, Katie Zacharia, left the role just five days into her tenure last month.

item.title: The only town in the U.S. that said yes to data centers
item.description: On Election Day, much of the country turned against the massive projects that power AI. Here’s why one place didn’t.

item.title: Why you end up coughing for weeks after a cold — and what to do about it
item.description: Experts share the habits and triggers to avoid, plus the remedies that could help alleviate a persistent hack following a respiratory infection.

item.title: Nvidia board to investigate CEO over relationship with suspected Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Sunday he had been unfaithful to his wife, and he apologized to the company and its customers.

item.title: Mysterious billionaire shows off ‘America’s oil’ — and Trump’s Venezuela
item.description: A visit to the petroleum-rich Orinoco Belt revealed a nascent U.S.-backed oil empire in a vassal state where officials once railed against the imperial north.

item.title: Golf has a drinking problem. There’s a new way around it.
item.description: For people in recovery, a round without booze can be a kind of spiritual practice.

item.title: Top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries says he’s a ‘hard yes’ on impeaching Pete Hegseth
item.description: Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is likely to become House speaker, said on ABC’s “This Week” that “Pete Hegseth has got to go.” Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) has said he plans to introduce a resolution as early as Monday calling for an impeachment vote on the defense secretary.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: She says no to angry in-law at holidays. Her husband is distraught.
item.description: Letter writer is refusing to host aggressive brother-in-law for holidays, and husband worries this will “break up his family.”

item.title: In the Mississippi Delta, a fight to make every vote count for Scott Colom
item.description: A group of young Black women helped Democrat Scott Colom do the unthinkable, potentially flipping a deep-red Senate seat.

item.title: Democrats won the midterms. Republicans may have won something bigger.
item.description: Social Security and Medicare will force painful choices for the party in control.

item.title: Potential JD Vance challengers smell blood in the water after GOP losses
item.description: The vice president has not made up his mind on running for president in 2028. His possible rivals, however, are wasting little time to prepare.

item.title: A Trump-era debate reignites: Has MAGA face gone too far?
item.description: The faces of women in the president’s orbit have become political Rorschach tests.

item.title: The moment a Statue of Liberty tour guide stopped pretending everything was okay
item.description: Isabelle Garbani won rave reviews for telling visitors about America’s immigration history. The problem was dealing with the present.

item.title: Hair loss, confusion and constant fatigue signaled a life-threatening condition
item.description: After waking up confused and barely able to speak, she was told by emergency room doctors to see a therapist for stress, but the problem was much more complex.

item.title: Israeli president taps ex-general Gadi Eisenkot, opponent of Netanyahu, to form government
item.description: The former military chief has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible extension of up to 14 more. If he fails, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is likely to get his chance.

item.title: A landmark study was flawed. Now my mother is losing her memory.
item.description: My mom gave up her hormone-replacement therapy. I wonder if things could have been different.

item.title: Laura Loomer, a Trump ally and activist, was paid thousands for political tweets, people familiar say
item.description: People familiar with the arrangements allege pay-to-play business practices by one of President Donald Trump's biggest online acolytes. The Washington Post reviewed bank transaction emails and a wire transfer statement that appear to show payments.

item.title: Trump’s wounded presidency turns to two unresolved wars, David Ignatius writes
item.description: Elections have consequences overseas, too.

item.title: Trump officials weigh major overhaul of National Park Service, Fish and Wildlife
item.description: An overhaul of the agencies would follow a similar move at the U.S. Forest Service.

item.title: Trump’s promotion of Stephen Miller unleashes fear, astonishment in industries reeling from immigration enforcement
item.description: Some leaders of groups representing the agriculture and construction sectors were gobsmacked after President Donald Trump named Miller, his chief architect of deportations, the new White House chief of staff.

item.title: Columnist Monica Hesse has found the most perimenopausal show on television
item.description: In the fourth season of the Julian Fellowes period drama “The Gilded Age,” women of a certain age aren’t fretting over hot flashes. Instead, these middle-aged baddies are scheming and wielding social power.

item.title: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis planning another White House run
item.description: Florida’s status as one of the few red states to mostly withstand the Democratic midterm sweep will be a core part of his argument, an adviser said.

item.title: Republicans took them for granted. Democrats wrote them off. No more.
item.description: What the midterms proved about the ‘God gap.’

item.title: Cornell faculty senate votes no confidence in university leadership
item.description: The symbolic vote comes in the aftermath of sexual assault allegations made by a former student.

item.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff
item.description: President Donald Trump's current White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, is leaving her post.

item.title: You may be able to fire your internet provider for a cheaper, better option
item.description: Americans usually rely on cable or fiber for their at-home internet. But there's a third option that many may find attractive.

item.title: I removed my fallopian tubes. What if my stepmom asks for grandkids? Our Say More writers are giving advice.
item.description: Maura Judkis and Amy Parlapiano are answering reader questions.

item.title: Two top Justice Department officials resign, including the head of the national security division
item.description: John Eisenberg resigned, along with Jason Reding Quiñones, the head of the U.S. attorney’s office in Miami. That office is leading a conspiracy investigation into several of President Donald Trump’s foes. The two officials are the latest high-profile departures from the administration since the midterm elections.

item.title: Corporate America courted Trump. Now a blitz of Democratic investigations is coming.
item.description: Democrats are preparing for congressional inquiries into some of the country’s largest companies, according to people familiar with the plan, setting off a scramble among executives with close ties to President Donald Trump and his administration.

item.title: President JD Vance? More slogging through a sewer of odious politics.
item.description: Temperate Americans of all political stripes should unite to stymie the vice president’s ambitions.

item.title: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, showing surprising strength
item.description: The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent, near the same low levels over the past year, according to a Labor Department report.

item.title: Jay Rockefeller, who served as West Virginia governor and a five-term U.S. senator, dies at 89
item.description: John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, an heir to a vast oil fortune and a liberal Democrat who became a leading voice on health care and national security died Friday at his home in Washington, D.C. His family did not provide a cause.

item.title: Pete Hegseth. Senate races. Trump’s arch. Tumbling stocks. Death row. Heart risks. Calorific coffee. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Judge halts construction on Trump’s planned arch shortly after a federal panel approved it to proceed
item.description: U.S. District Judge Tanya S. Chutkan blocked the project, siding with military veterans and local government officials who had urged her to stop it. Opponents of the proposed arch say it is illegal and needs to be approved by the current Congress.

item.title: Federal panel led by Trump allies approves 250-foot arch, clearing the way for construction as a judge weighs whether to halt it
item.description: The National Capital Planning Commission gave final authorization for the memorial after more than eight hours of public testimony and heated debate. Over 120 people, including architects, historians and military veterans, urged administration officials not to proceed, saying the project would wrongly overshadow nearby Arlington National Cemetery and irrevocably change the Washington landscape.

item.title: New estrogen research may change how scientists think about women’s aging brains
item.description: Scientists are assessing the potential benefits of hormone therapy for older women’s cognition.
